earnings.title: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
highlights: Sharp focus on operational efficiency resulted in strong consolidated net income performance of $5.3 billion, up 5.2 percent year-over-year.
Earnings per share (EPS) was $1.25, up 6.8 percent year-over-year, driving Adjusted EPS¹ of $1.31, up 8.3 percent year-over-year.
Acquired nearly 1.7 million mobility and broadband subscribers in the first nine months of 2026, compared to 879,000 in the first nine months of 2025.
Cash flow from operating activities was $11.5 billion for the quarter, representing an increase of 2.2 percent year-over-year.
This supported free cash flow¹ of $7.8 billion, up 12.1 percent year-over-year.

quotes.text: Verizon delivered another record-breaking quarter. One year into our transformation, Verizon is fundamentally stronger — operationally, financially, and competitively.

outlook: Mobility and broadband service revenue of $23.5 billion grew 2.9 percent year-over-year, up sequentially and forecast to grow approximately 4.0 percent in fourth-quarter 2026.
The company continues to anticipate total fiber passings to exceed 32 million by year-end, remaining on track toward a target of 40 to 50 million fiber passings over the medium term.
The company continues to expect to repurchase up to $4.5 billion for the full year.
Postpaid phone net additions: 1.1 million to 1.2 million, up from upper half of 750,000 to 1.0 million, representing an increase of more than three times compared to 2025.

items.heading: We face significant competition that may negatively affect our operating results.

If we are not able to take advantage of developments in technology and address changing consumer demand on a timely basis, we may experience a decline in the demand for our services, be unable to implement our business strategy and experience reduced profits.

Adverse conditions in the U.S. and international economies, changes to international trade and tariff policies and related economic and geopolitical factors could impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Cyberattacks impacting our networks or systems could have an adverse effect on our business.
Our long-term success depends on our ability to implement business transformation initiatives and achieve their anticipated benefits.
System failures and disruptions to our networks and operations could prevent us from providing reliable service to customers and adversely affect our business.
